conventions: The doxology כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ (7.3, 7.6) divides as כִּי → for, לְ → 'endureth for' (copula on the prepositional predicate, rules 20/49, headed on for), עוֹלָם → ever, חֶסֶד → lovingkindness, suffix → his. In 7.3 the supplied 'he' of 'For he is good' resumes the יהוה written earlier in the verse and joins that name's unit under rule 25, headed on Jehovah; 'saying' there is a supplied lexical verb with no לֵאמֹר and is added. 7.6 writes no such pronoun.
report: Checked every multi-treatment bucket in the candidate table against the verses. None is a split: every difference is licensed by what the ASV wrote — the bare apodosis of 7.1 against the 'then' of 7.14/18/20; articles left unrepresented only where a demonstrative, a possessive suffix, a bare rendering ('heaven', 'king Solomon', 'by night', 'peoples') or an agreement slot takes the phrase's determiner; לְ silenced only in the modal complement of 7.2, the coordinated bare 'do' of 7.17, לֵאמֹר, the resultative 'make it a proverb' of 7.20, the topicalized לְכָל־עֹבֵר of 7.21 and the bare-object datives; the possessive recastings 'Jehovah's house', 'the king's house', 'Solomon's heart' handled identically under rule 29 in 7.2 and 7.11.

Recurring constructions agree across verses: לִפְנֵי fused and headed on the construct (7.4, 7.7, 7.17, 7.19), with the copula joining the fusion in 7.7; 'give/gave thanks' headed on thanks (7.3, 7.6); the refrain כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ divided the same way in 7.3 and 7.6; בַּיּוֹם/לַחֹדֶשׁ + ordinal with the assimilated article taking 'the' and the agreement article unrepresented (7.9, 7.10); בַּעֵת הַהִיא and every הַ…הַזֶּה phrase giving the determiner to the demonstrative (7.8, 7.12, 7.15, 7.16, 7.20, 7.21, 7.22); מֵעַל → 'out of' twice in 7.20 headed alike.

The four added units were read end to end: 'their' (7.3, no suffix on אַפַּיִם), 'saying' (7.3, no לֵאמֹר), 'that is made' (7.15, rule 20's חֲמַס אֶרֶץ → 'violence done' boundary inside a nominal recasting), 'as for' (7.17, fronted pronoun with no marker). No verse folds a comparable supply into a neighbouring morpheme, so the table's blind spot hides nothing.

Single-verse judgments that a later reader may want to weigh, none of them splits and none changed: 7.14 gives 'by' to עַל where rule 33's agent-by before a bare nominal with a passive participle could instead give it to שֵׁם and leave עַל unrepresented; 7.15 places the relative of 'the prayer that is made' in the added run rather than in תְּפִלָּה's unit under rule 46's closing paragraph; 7.5 keeps the 'a' of 'a hundred' with the numeral as the English numeral's own word rather than as a determiner of 'sheep'.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention: 23 articles, 12 prepositions and the object marker of 7.11 under rules 16, 29, 40 and 41; the apodosis waw of 7.1 under rule 14; the בְּ of בָּחַר בְּ in 7.12 under rule 40; the resumptive suffix of 7.14 under rule 22; the paragogic nun of 7.19 under rule 32. No genuine error among them.
Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already states; no promotion or amendment.
